title: The wand bank
steps: Eldra holds her lost book again, after so many years.
I thank thee, kind {wizard}. Thou hast brought much joy to this old spirit today.
She drifts away between the shelves, reading as she goes.
At the end of the aisle, just past the last shelf, is the wand bank: a counter where a pupil's parent lends you a school wand for the year.
You made it! Oh, is that your new school wand? It looks perfect for you!
It is! And here is your spare wand back, {friend}. Thank you so much for lending it to me.

You have learned so much in the library! You know how to use a name for a value, which programmers call a variable, and how to use `print` to see what a thing knows, its attribute. You also caught what a method gives back using `find_nearest`, kept it in a variable, and used `give`. You even opened a door with its own method, `door.open()`, after picking up its key, and cast the *fendra* spell to draw things from the shelves right to you!
Night is falling outside. I heard the older pupils whisper that the passages change after dark... I wonder who walks there at night?
